questions.text: Consider a system with 2 level cache. Access times of Level 1 cache, Level 2 cache and main memory are 1 ns, 10 ns, and 500 ns respectively. The hit rates of Level 1 and Level 2 caches are 0.8 and 0.9, respectively. What is the average access time of the system ignoring the search time within the cache?
questions.solution:
Hierarchical access:
[latex]0.8\times1+0.2\times0.9\times10+0.2\times0.1\times500=0.8+1.8+10=12.6[/latex] ns

Answer: 12.6

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Relative mode of addressing is most relevant to writing:
questions.solution:
Relative (PC-relative) addressing gives addresses as an offset from the current instruction, so the code works wherever it is loaded: position-independent code.

Answer: Position - independent code

questions.text: In which class of Flynn's taxanomy, Von Neumann architecture belongs to?
questions.solution:
A von Neumann machine executes one instruction stream on one data stream: SISD (Single Instruction, Single Data).

Answer: SISD

questions.text: Register renaming is done in pipelined processors:
questions.solution:
Register renaming gives each new value its own physical register, which removes false dependencies (WAR and WAW hazards) in the pipeline.

Answer: to handle certain kinds of hazards
